request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

A parallel plate capacitor is filled with a dielectric whose dielectric constant varies with the applied voltage as K = α V , where α = 1 volt ^(− 1) . Another identical capacitor (without dielectric) charged to a potential drop V_0 = 30 volt is connected in parallel to the first uncharged capacitor. The final potential drop across each capacitor is
(A) 5 V
(B) 10 V
(C) 15 V
(D) 20 V

result.working:
Let C0 be the capacitance of the plain capacitor. The dielectric-filled one has C = K·C0 = αV·C0 at voltage V.
Total initial charge = C0·V0 = 30C0 (the dielectric capacitor starts uncharged).
After connection both are at the same V, so charge conservation gives C0·V + (αV·C0)·V = 30C0.
With α = 1 V⁻¹ this becomes V² + V − 30 = 0, i.e. (V + 6)(V − 5) = 0.
Taking the positive root, V = 5 V.
result.note: This uses the standard approach Q = C(V)·V, where the capacitance is evaluated at the final voltage.
